content.title: Gesture Collection | Intangible Traces Form a Core and Rewrite the Environment
content.summary: Show an adult's empty hands and an ordinary environment before defining a collection vessel with both palms. Draw traces only from that environment into one graspable core, release it once along a fixed axis, and hold the redistributed material as a visible environmental response.

quick_start.input_format: adult subject in an ordinary environment first proves both hands empty + palms define a stable collection vessel + traces from at least three environmental points converge into one core + one gesture releases the same material along an established axis + material redistributes through the same environment and holds a visible response
quick_start.recommended_input: An adult acoustic engineer stops in an empty station and clearly shows both hands empty. Vibration lines from rails, cables, and panels compress into one amber glass pulse between the palms; one release sends rings across the station until suspended cables stop swaying.
required_anchors: Show one adult, ordinary environment and visibly empty hands before collection.
Form one stable two-hand collection volume before traces appear.
Use exactly one release gesture and preserve the core's material identity along one axis.
Distribute the released material back across the same environment and hold the response.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Show an adult's empty hands and an ordinary environment before defining a collection vessel with both palms. Draw traces only from that environment into one graspable core, release it once along a fixed axis, and hold the redistributed material as a visible environmental response.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish one original clearly adult subject moving through an ordinary environment with both hands visibly empty. Let the adult stop and shape one stable collection volume with both palms before any visible phenomenon appears. Draw fine related traces from at least three surrounding environmental locations toward that volume, keep them materially continuous, and compress them into one single manipulable core. Use exactly one release gesture to send the same core away from the hands along an established spatial axis. Expand that material back into the environment as a distributed, readable response while the original location and adult remain identifiable. The reusable mechanism is empty-hand baseline, gesture-defined collection volume, environmental convergence, single-core compression, one release and distributed world response—not the source man, face, clothing, street, light strands, orb design, city, trees, exact hand motion, camera, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Show one adult, ordinary environment and visibly empty hands before collection.
invariants.purpose: Creates proof that the phenomenon is acquired rather than pre-held.
invariants.ablation_failure: An existing prop removes the intangible-to-tangible conversion.

invariants.rule: Form one stable two-hand collection volume before traces appear.
invariants.purpose: Gives invisible material a spatial destination.
invariants.ablation_failure: Changing hand shapes make convergence unreadable.

invariants.rule: Pull continuous related traces from at least three environmental sources into one core.
invariants.purpose: Binds the material to the world and shows accumulation.
invariants.ablation_failure: Particles appearing only at the palms look conjured without collection.

invariants.rule: Use exactly one release gesture and preserve the core's material identity along one axis.
invariants.purpose: Makes the reversal causal and trackable.
invariants.ablation_failure: Multiple throws or an unrelated object break conservation.

invariants.rule: Distribute the released material back across the same environment and hold the response.
invariants.purpose: Completes the collection-release cycle at world scale.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending on the orb alone leaves no environmental consequence.
